chapter: Coming up in New York and Harlem theatres
title: Leading his own bands in Harlem, the Chapman execution night and Casper's
summary: Barred from the Clef Club, Whaley builds his own band, plays a Harlem Italian place on gangster Gerald Chapman's execution night, and recalls Small's opening and Casper's.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: He had all the gigs, like the Clef Club. If you get in the Clef Club, you are already made, but they didn't want no outsiders in there. They wouldn't let me in there, so finally I got the break with Lucky and I started doing a whole lot of things then. I got myself a band and used to play over in Brooklyn, Cat's Meow, I used to play all over and then I had a job on 131st Street at the -- the Italians had the place there and the night Gerald Chapman was electrocuted --
Gerald Chapman, he was a big gangster.
Did they put him in the electric chair.

Yeah, he was captured up there in Connecticut, see and I had never seen so many $100 bills come in a place, all that week trying to save this guy. They had so much money there, they couldn't buy him off, and so the night of the electrocution, the man said, play nothing but 'The Prisoner's Song' and that's all I played, 'The Prisoner's Song' and then from there I went -- I used to go up to 136th Street there, they had another joint where I used to go up there and play and get acquainted with the people and in '25 Small's opened on 135th Street.
What was the name of that place, Tom.
Casper's, you know the gangsters -- he was the head of the number racket there in New York. Casper. And they kidnapped him.
So what happened up there. Used to work up there.
Yeah, I used to go up there. Play up there for awhile.
